theater: 布加勒斯特城區與瓦拉幾亞南部

battle.name: 瓦拉幾亞1848年革命
battle.theater: 布加勒斯特城區與瓦拉幾亞南部
battle.brief: 一八四八年六月，瓦拉幾亞青年軍官在布加勒斯特聚會，朗讀以比利時憲法為藍本的革命憲章，民兵隨即與親王衛隊交火，逼親王退位並成立革命議會。七月南部農民起義擴散，八月之後鄂圖曼與俄羅斯聯軍南下，九月下旬入城，議會在十一月解散，代表向親王宣誓。民兵手中的雷管步槍在街壘上撐了半年。

kit.name: 雷管步槍
kit.history: 雷管取代火燧之後，底火在霧裡也打得響。射程變長，隊形就散了。

countries: 交戰的一方是瓦拉幾亞親王的政府與守備軍：親王是鄂圖曼蘇丹的封臣，首都布加勒斯特有一支規模不大的常備守備隊，以及由克里特與阿爾巴尼亞人組成的親王衛隊，駐在總督府與城門一帶；鄂圖曼在多瑙河兩岸的駐軍也可以隨時北上。另一方是首都民兵與秘密社團「兄弟會」的網絡：「兄弟會」在一八四〇年代中期由一批年輕軍官與學生組成，核心人物有伊昂·吉卡、康斯坦丁·羅塞蒂與科斯塔切·基里亞克；其外圍是各街區的首都民兵、青年團體、手工行會武裝，以及六月之後南下支援的農民隊伍。鄉村地主與部分貴族站在親王一邊，試圖以保留君主制的名義換取外力保護。國外介入者包括鄂圖曼帝國、俄羅斯帝國，以及一八四八年夏天從希臘本土渡海而來的數百名希臘革命軍，他們以方陣編隊加入革命軍，與親王軍在布加勒斯特外圍交鋒。指揮體系方面，革命一方的最高機構是革命委員會與民意代表大會，主席團由羅塞蒂、吉卡與戈列斯庫家族的幾位成員輪替；保皇一方的核心是親王與數名受英國支持的閣員，外加鄂圖曼使節的干預。
countriesEn: One side was the government and garrison of the Wallachian prince, who was a vassal of the Ottoman sultan: Bucharest had a small permanent garrison together with a princely guard recruited among Cretan and Albanian men, stationed at the court and the city gates, while the Ottoman troops stationed along the Danube could always march north. The other side was the capital militia and the network of the secret society called the Brotherhood, formed in the middle of the 1840s by a group of young officers and students, with Ioan Ghica, Costache Rosetti and Costache Chiriac at its centre; around them stood the district militias of the capital, youth groups, the armed bands of the guilds, and, after the revolution broke out, the peasant columns that marched south. Village landowners and part of the boyar aristocracy sided with the prince, hoping to save the monarchy in exchange for outside protection. The foreign actors were the Ottoman Empire, Russia, and several hundred Greek revolutionaries who crossed from Greece in the summer of 1848 and joined the revolutionary army in phalanx formation. On the revolutionary side the highest organs were the revolutionary committee and the assembly of the people's deputies, whose presidium rotated among Rosetti, Ghica and members of the Golescu family; on the conservative side the core was the prince together with a few ministers backed by Britain and with the constant mediation of the Ottoman envoy.
people: 伊昂·吉卡在一八四八年六月十四日於科斯塔切·基里亞克宅中起草並公開朗讀那份以比利時憲法為藍本的革命憲章，隨後被視為革命的政治領袖，他也在革命委員會中擔任要職，革命失敗後被捕，長期流亡在外。康斯坦丁·羅塞蒂是報人與革命委員會成員，革命期間主持民意的宣傳與議會工作，事後被囚禁並流放到修道院。安東·布拉替亞努當時正在獄中，透過家人與外界保持聯繫，日後成為一八五九年兩公國合併的推動者；西米翁·巴爾努丘與亞歷山德魯·伊萬·庫扎等人把特蘭西瓦尼亞的思想帶入首都，也在革命機構中任職。阿列克·戈蘭自巴黎歸國，把二月的消息與報紙帶回布加勒斯特，是引爆行動的直接推手。希臘方面，老兵馬基里揚尼斯以將軍身分加入革命軍，率領的方陣是革命軍中少數受過統一訓練的兵力。親王一邊有喬治·比貝斯庫與巴布·迪米特里·斯特爾貝伊兩位親王，前者被迫退位、後者靠外軍支持復位；彼得拉切·波埃納魯是親王軍的指揮官，六月的失利之後被親王下令處決。
peopleEn: Ioan Ghica drafted and publicly read the revolutionary constitution, modelled on the Belgian constitution, on 14 June 1848 in the house of Costache Chiriac; he was afterwards regarded as the political leader of the revolution and held a seat on the revolutionary committee, and after the defeat he was arrested and spent long years in exile. Costache Rosetti, a journalist and member of the revolutionary committee, ran the propaganda and the parliamentary work of the revolution and was afterwards imprisoned and exiled to a monastery. Anton Bratanu was in prison at the time and kept in contact with the movement through his family; he would later drive the union of the two principalities. Simion Barnutiu and Alexandru Ioan Cuza brought Transylvanian ideas into the capital and also served in the revolutionary institutions. Alecu Goran, back from Paris, carried the news of February and the newspapers to Bucharest and was the direct cause of the action being taken. On the Greek side the veteran Makriyannis joined the revolutionary army as a general, and his phalanx was one of the few bodies in the revolutionary force that had received regular training. On the princely side there were two princes, Gheorghe Bibescu, who was forced to abdicate, and Barbu Dimitrie Stirbei, who was restored with the help of foreign troops. Petrace Poenaru commanded the prince's forces and was executed on the prince's orders after the defeats of June.
kits: 瓦拉幾亞民兵與政府軍使用的火器相當駁雜：守備隊與親王衛隊多為舊式燧發滑膛火槍與手槍，配克里特式的彎刀；首都民兵則大量使用獵槍、短管散彈槍與本地打造的長槍，其中一部分在一八四〇年代中期改裝成雷管擊發，正是本卡所指的雷管步槍：改底火、排擊錘、加強槍機，使射手在清晨、黃昏與火藥煙霧裡也能立刻擊發，不必在濕冷天候裡浪費時間重新點火。彈藥供應是最大的瓶頸：本地幾乎不產雷管與紙殼彈，獵槍彈與軍用彈的直徑不合，多數民兵只備有極少數發，裝藥量全憑射手的經驗。砲兵方面，革命軍在布加勒斯特城門與市集一帶只有少量舊式攻城砲與臼砲，數目少而射程有限，親王一方則可從鄂圖曼邊境取得較新的雷管砲。冷兵器並未退出：長矛、鐮刀、獵刀與農具在街壘與村落戰中大量使用，因為對沒有火槍的人而言，長柄農具與短管獵槍一樣致命。馬匹只夠給親王的騎兵與幾名軍官，革命軍的移動全靠步行，農民隊伍的行軍速度因此成為補給線上的關鍵變數。
kitsEn: The firearms of the Wallachian militia and government troops were a mixed lot: the garrison and the princely guard carried old flintlock smoothbore muskets and pistols with Cretan-style curved swords, while the capital militia used sporting guns, short scatterguns and locally made long guns in quantity, a part of which had been converted to percussion in the middle of the 1840s. That converted weapon is precisely the percussion rifle of this card: a new nipple on the stock, a new hammer, a stronger lock, so that a man could fire in the early morning, at dusk and in the smoke of black powder without wasting time relighting a match. Ammunition was the real bottleneck. The country produced neither percussion caps nor paper cartridges, sporting bullets and service bullets did not fit the same bore, and most militiamen carried a handful of rounds apiece, the charge being a matter of guesswork. On the artillery side the revolutionaries had only a few old siege pieces and mortars at the gates and markets of Bucharest, few in number and short in range, while the prince's side could draw newer percussion guns from the Ottoman frontier. Cold weapons had not disappeared either: pikes, sickles, hunting knives and farm tools were used in quantity in the barricades and in village fighting, because for a man without a musket a long-handled tool was as lethal as a short sporting gun. Horses were enough only for the prince's cavalry and a few officers; the revolutionaries moved on foot, and the marching speed of the peasant columns was therefore the variable that decided the supply line.
tactics: 首都民兵採鬆散的街區營制，每個街區自行選出指揮官，遇到戰鬥才臨時集合；集合速度慢，陣形卻極難被砲火一次打散。革命初期的主要手段是夜襲與街壘：民團封鎖通往親王宮的街道，把家具、石塊與車輛堆成胸牆，射手藏在後方屋頂與閣樓，以獵槍居高射擊，使親王的正規步兵無法展開。十四日的憲章宣讀與宣誓同時是一場政治集會，也是集結點名，之後民兵在城門一帶與親王衛隊正面相撞。農民隊伍南下之後轉為移動戰：以一兩百人為一隊的縱隊沿鄉間小路推進，遇敵即散，避免被騎兵與砲兵消滅。親王與鄂圖曼聯軍反過來用制式化方法：白晝進攻、夜間設防，佔領制高點與水壩、橋頭這類要道，切斷革命軍彼此的聯繫；最後以聯軍進入首都、包圍議會大廈、斷絕議會對外聯絡的做法，把一場革命壓成一次外交投降。武器庫與城門的控制權，在整場衝突中比正面交火更能決定勝負。
tacticsEn: The capital militia was organised loosely by district, each quarter choosing its own officers and assembling only when there was a fight to fight; the assembly was slow, but the resulting formation was very hard to break with artillery in one stroke. The first methods of the revolution were night attacks and barricades. The militia closed the streets leading to the princely court, piled furniture, stone and carts into breastworks, and posted shooters in the roofs and lofts behind them, so that the prince's regular infantry could not deploy. The reading of the constitution and the oath of 14 June were at once a political meeting and a muster, after which the militia collided with the princely guard at the gates of the city. Once the peasant columns moved south they turned to mobile war: bands of a hundred or two hundred men pushed along country lanes, dispersed on contact, and avoided being destroyed by cavalry and guns. The prince and his Ottoman allies used the opposite, regular method: advance by day, entrench by night, seize the heights and the dykes and the heads of bridges, and cut the revolutionaries off from one another. In the end the allies entered the capital, surrounded the hall where the assembly sat and severed its links with the outside world, and a revolution was converted into a diplomatic surrender. Control of the arsenals and the city gates decided more than any pitched battle during these months.
data: 這場戰爭的數字在當時的報紙與後來的回憶錄中差異頗大，可以確定的有幾點。首都民兵在冊人數以萬計，多數只有獵槍與農具；親王的常備守備隊規模僅數百人，加上克里特與阿爾巴尼亞營也不過千人上下。希臘方陣的規模在數百至兩千之間，史料多記為一千五百上下。革命軍在南方的農民隊伍為數千人，農民起義被鎮壓時，各方記載的死亡數從數百到數千都有，最保守的說法是村莊被焚、馬匹與農具大量損失，數以百計的武裝者陣亡。鄂圖曼與俄羅斯的聯軍在九月下旬進入首府時，投入的兵力為數千人，另有海運與多瑙河航運支援。九月之後革命議會被解散，十一月在科特羅切尼的宣誓儀式上，代表們一個個上前向親王宣誓效忠，這一場面本身沒有傷亡。較能核實的是日期：六月十四日憲章宣讀、六月中旬城內民兵與親王軍的衝突、七月南部農民起義、九月下旬聯軍入城、十一月議會解散與宣誓，先後次序明確。
dataEn: The figures for this conflict differ considerably between the newspapers of the day and the memoirs written later, but a few things can be established. The capital militia numbered thousands on paper, most of them with nothing but a sporting gun and a farm tool; the prince's permanent garrison was only a few hundred strong, and even with the Cretan and Albanian companies the princely field force stayed around a thousand. The Greek phalanx is given in the sources as anywhere from several hundred to two thousand, most often about fifteen hundred. The peasant columns in the south ran to several thousand men, and when the rising was crushed the accounts of the dead range from hundreds to thousands; the most conservative reading is that villages were burned, horses and tools were lost in bulk, and several hundred armed men were killed. The Ottoman and Russian allies entered the capital in the second half of September with a few thousand men, supported by sea traffic and by navigation on the Danube. After September the revolutionary assembly was dissolved, and in the ceremony at Cotroceni in November the deputies came forward one by one to swear allegiance to the prince; that ceremony itself cost no lives. The dates are the most verifiable part: the reading of the constitution on 14 June, the clashes between the capital militia and the prince's troops in mid-June, the peasant rising in July, the entry of the allied troops into the capital in late September, and the dissolution and oath of the assembly in November all follow one another in a clear order.
cause: 一八四八年三月，法國二月革命的消息傳到布加勒斯特，巴黎學成歸國的年輕軍官阿列克·戈蘭把報紙與口信帶回城內，使「兄弟會」決定立即行動，這是直接引爆點。更深的根源在瓦拉幾亞社會本身：國家的行政、稅收與教會多由希臘裔或外來人掌管，農村的土地問題懸而未決，一八四七年農民暴動的餘波仍在，比薩拉比亞、布拉索夫等地的手工行會要求代表權與廢除特權；親王的改革派政府試圖以向外國借款取得短期喘息，反而加深了對外來勢力的怨恨。統治集團內部的分裂同樣致命：改革派的青年軍官與親王的保守派彼此不容，「白社」與「紅社」在特蘭西瓦尼亞策動，並以「兄弟會」的名義串連瓦拉幾亞，一旦瓦拉幾亞成功，兩邊都相信可以借勢而起。對外，鄂圖曼蘇丹在意的不是改革內容，而是這場革命會否把瓦拉幾亞的內政變成俄羅斯或奧地利介入的藉口；英國則明確支持保住親王的既有框架。以上各方拉扯，使革命在爆發時就已經內定了一個結局：只要帝國的槍口介入，首都的街壘撐不了多久。
causeEn: In March 1848 the news of the February revolution in France reached Bucharest, and Alecu Goran, a young officer educated in Paris, brought back the newspapers and the messages, which persuaded the Brotherhood to act at once; that was the immediate spark. The deeper causes lay in Wallachian society itself. Administration, taxation and the church were largely in the hands of Greeks and other outsiders, the land question in the villages remained unresolved, the after-effects of the peasant disturbances of 1847 were still fresh, and the guilds of the towns asked for representation and the abolition of privileges. The prince's reforming government tried to buy breathing space by borrowing from foreign creditors and in doing so deepened the resentment of foreign influence. The split inside the ruling group was just as fatal: the reformist young officers and the prince's conservatives could not live with each other, while the White and Red societies worked in Transylvania and tied themselves to Wallachia through the Brotherhood, each side believing that a success in Bucharest would be its own opportunity. Abroad, what the Ottoman Porte cared about was not the content of the reforms but whether the revolution would provide a pretext for Russian or Austrian intervention; Britain, for its part, openly supported keeping the prince's existing framework intact. Such were the pulls and pushes, and the outcome was already settled at the moment the revolution broke out: once the guns of an empire intervened, the barricades of the capital could not hold for long.
impact: 革命雖然失敗，卻留下幾條長線。廢除特權與土地歸還的條款雖未實行，卻成了日後一八六四年瓦拉幾亞農民起義的直接口號；「兄弟會」的成員在往後十五年裡成為自由派的核心，其中數人在一八五九年兩公國合併時身居要職，而瓦拉幾亞革命領袖的弟弟當時正是在獄中度過那些年。土地問題的懸置、對外國干預的敏感，以及各公國之間行政與政治體制的分歧，全部被帶進一八六〇年代，最終在一八六六年布加勒斯特會議後寫成羅馬尼亞小公國的憲法。軍事上，這次革命是鄂圖曼帝國在巴爾幹使用聯軍干預的一次示範，此後數十年俄奧兩國在東方問題上屢次援引類似的干預模式；守備軍使用的雷管步槍與少量攻城砲也顯示，首都民兵在面對配備更完整的外軍時，除了街壘與射擊精度之外並無其他籌碼。對國際觀感而言，這場革命讓歐洲注意到多瑙河公國正在成為俄國與奧地利爭奪的棋盤。
impactEn: The revolution failed, yet it left several long lines running. The clauses on the abolition of privileges and the return of the land were never carried out, but they became the direct slogan of the Wallachian peasant rising of 1864. The members of the Brotherhood formed the core of the liberal party over the following fifteen years, and several of them held key posts when the two principalities were united in 1859, the brother of one of the revolution's leaders having spent those very years in prison. The unresolved land question, the sensitivity to foreign intervention, and the divergence of administrative and political structures between the principalities were all carried into the 1860s and were finally written into the constitution of the small Romanian state after the Bucharest conference of 1866. Militarily, this revolution was a demonstration of Ottoman intervention in the Balkans with combined forces, a pattern invoked again and again by Russia and Austria in the Eastern Question for decades afterwards. The percussion muskets and the handful of siege pieces of the garrison also showed that, faced with an invading army equipped more completely, the capital militia had nothing to rely on but barricades and the accuracy of its shooting. For the wider public the revolution also made plain to Europe that the Danubian principalities had become a board on which Russia and Austria played.
result: 十四日的憲章宣讀使革命在政治上一開始就取得主動，民兵入城、議會成立、土地條款宣告，節節推進到七月的農民起義與南部戰事；但八月之後鄂圖曼帝國在瓦拉幾亞的支持者重新集結，九月下旬聯軍進入布加勒斯特，包圍議會大廈，切斷議會與外界的聯絡。議會在十一月解散，代表們在科特羅切尼向親王宣誓效忠，革命議會所通過的憲法被中止；伊昂·吉卡、康斯坦丁·羅塞蒂等領袖被捕，囚禁後流放，彼得拉切·波埃納魯等親王軍的指揮官則在六月的失利後被親王下令處決。農民起義被殘酷平定，村莊被焚，農民武裝的損失慘重。此後瓦拉幾亞恢復親王統治，財政與人事回到保守派手中，國家對外國干預的防備反而更強；革命所提出的土地與特權問題未獲解決，留待下一代人重提。
resultEn: The reading of the constitution on the fourteenth gave the revolution the initiative from the start: the militia entered the capital, the assembly was formed, the clause on the land was proclaimed, and the movement advanced by stages through the peasant rising and the fighting in the south in July. But after August the Ottoman supporters of the prince in Wallachia gathered again, and in the second half of September the allied troops entered Bucharest, surrounded the hall where the assembly met and cut the assembly off from the outside world. In November the assembly was dissolved, the deputies swore allegiance to the prince at Cotroceni, and the constitution passed by the revolutionary assembly was suspended. Ioan Ghica and Costache Rosetti were arrested, imprisoned and then exiled, while commanders of the prince's army such as Petrace Poenaru were executed on the prince's orders after the defeats of June. The peasant rising was crushed with great severity, villages were burned and the armed peasant bands suffered heavy losses. Wallachia returned to princely rule, its finances and appointments to the conservatives, and the state's defences against foreign interference grew stricter rather than looser. The land and privilege questions raised in 1848 were left unanswered for the next generation to take up.
